scenes.title: Gobron [vue d'un moteur]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol from 1912, held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France (Estampes et photographie department, EI-13 (175)), showing a view of an engine of a Gobron. It is a negative glass plate photograph, 13 x 18 cm or larger, in the public domain.
scenes.explanation: Aerosol spray cans with modern solvents and propellants did not exist in 1912, making this can impossible in the photograph.

scenes.title: [Ligne de personnes couchées le long des berges]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol, dated 1911, shows a line of people lying down along the banks of the Seine in France. The record identifies it as a bathing scene in Paris.
scenes.explanation: Clear PET plastic bottles did not exist in 1911, so a transparent molded bottle with a screw cap could not be present.

scenes.title: [Variante du premier projet de baldaquin]
scenes.description: A 1705 drawing by Robert de Cotte, held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, shows a variant of the first project for a baldachin, rendered in pen and brown ink with brown wash. It is an elevation from a collection of baldachins for the decoration of various unidentified altars.
scenes.explanation: LED desk lamps did not exist in 1705, as lighting relied on candles and oil lamps.

scenes.title: 17-9-22, concours de pêche à la ligne [les Sociétés de pêche défilant dans Paris]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol dated 17 September 1922 shows fishing societies parading in Paris during a fishing competition. The record identifies it as "concours de pêche à la ligne [les Sociétés de pêche défilant dans Paris]," meaning "fishing competition [the fishing societies parading in Paris]," and it is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
scenes.explanation: Telescoping aluminum selfie sticks with phone clamps did not exist in 1922, so this object cannot belong to the scene.
